one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent lacked the domain knowledge to design a multi-component CoreWars warrior, instead cycling through single-archetype strategies (scanner, imp, dwarf) that each fail against at least three of the five opponents, never achieving the required win rates.
t_err_evidence: At step 8, the agent writes its first warrior and simultaneously reveals two critical knowledge gaps: (1) it believes launching SPL/JMP at absolute addresses (e.g., 2000, 4000) will execute code located at those addresses, but no code is there; (2) it designs a single-strategy scanner when the task requires handling five diverse opponent archetypes, demonstrating it lacks knowledge of multi-module CoreWars design.
t_commit_evidence: By step 55, the agent has tested the basic imp against all five opponents and sees complete failure against paper (100% ties, 0 wins), snake (1 win/100), and g2-clear (0 wins/100). With 59% vs stone and 84% vs vampire, no single archetype can satisfy all requirements. Despite 116 steps remaining, the agent never conceptualizes a multi-component warrior and instead spends all remaining steps tuning dwarfs, imps, scanners, and superficial hybrids.
t_surface_evidence: At step 10, the first pmars run shows 'MultiScanner by AI Warrior scores 0 / Stone by mzvince (Everything2) scores 30 / Results: 0 10 0' - the warrior loses all 10 rounds against even the simplest opponent (stone), confirming the scanner design is completely non-functional.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks two key pieces of domain knowledge: (1) how Redcode addressing modes and SPL work (causing the early scanner failures from steps 8-28 where code is written expecting absolute-address-launched processes to execute non-existent code at those locations), and more critically (2) that meeting multi-opponent win-rate requirements in CoreWars requires specialized multi-module warriors rather than a single archetype. This knowledge gap causes the agent to spend the entire 171-step trajectory cycling through single-strategy approaches (scanner, imp, dwarf, hybrid-dwarf-imp) none of which can satisfy all five opponent requirements simultaneously.
forewarning_evidence: Step 10: 'MultiScanner by AI Warrior scores 0 / Stone scores 30 / Results: 0 10 0' - complete loss despite scanner design intended to counter stone. Steps 13, 16, 19, 21, 24, 26, 28: repeated scanner attempts all return 0 wins against stone with identical failure pattern. Step 26 shows a compilation error ('Improper placement of dat') revealing Redcode syntax ignorance. By step 40, even the reference paper.red only gets 5/50 wins vs stone, foreshadowing the difficulty but the agent doesn't update its strategy approach.
